elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Grant now reads "TrueLink hereby grants to Client and, upon written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates a non-exclusive license to use the Interface" — affiliates are within the grant, albeit conditioned on notice (the preferred position contemplates unconditional extension, so this is at the fallback formulation).

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: No reference to contractors, subcontractors, or persons acting on Client's behalf appears anywhere in the rendered grant; the drafter expressly declined to press this point.

The rendered § 2(a) grant states no duration and the term/fee provision (§ 2(c), described as subscription-style) is not in the record, so it cannot be determined whether a paid-up licence exists or is perpetual; no perpetuity language was added.

No "irrevocable" language was inserted and the fee/term structure (§ 2(c)) is outside the cited text, so the existence and revocability of a paid-up licence cannot be assessed from the operative language supplied.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Nothing in the rendered language limits termination of the licence to uncured material breach; the redline leaves the termination mechanic in § 2(c) untouched.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The new § 15 exception is limited to "Client's transfer of the license to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction"; it does not reach successors generally (e.g., asset sale, reorganisation, operation of law), so the broader preferred element is not satisfied.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink hereby grants to Client and, upon written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates a non-exclusive license..." — coverage of affiliates is triggered by written notice to Vendor, exactly the fallback mechanic. "Client" is defined as Mortgage Logic.com, Inc. alone (p0003), so this is new, non-duplicative coverage.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: § 15 now reads "...except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or for Client's transfer of the license to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction." The carve-out is Client-only and grants Vendor no new assignment exception.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: affiliate coverage on written notice is inserted directly into the § 2(a) grant, and a Client-only M&A-successor carve-out is added to the § 15 consent requirement. The finding is properly scored as a deviation because the unedited clause failed both fallback elements (no affiliate path, and all transfers of rights required TrueLink's approval).

Preferred level fails on contractors (no reference added), on the paid-up perpetual/irrevocable elements (cannot be assessed; § 2(c) term/fee text not supplied and no perpetuity or irrevocability wording inserted), on the material-breach-only termination limit (no such restriction anywhere), and on general successor transferability (the carve-out is confined to merger/acquisition successors). To reach the preferred level the drafter would need to add "and its contractors acting on its behalf" to the grant, state that paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable, limit revocation/termination of the subscription licence to uncured material breach, and broaden the § 15 carve-out from "a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction" to "any successor to Client's business or assets".

Minimality holds: only two surgical insertions were made, both inside the target elements. No survival tail, expense language, procedure, or boilerplate was added; the pre-existing Customer-favourable non-exclusivity/free-to-use-alternatives sentence and the mutual affiliate assignment exception are retained untouched. The retained mutual affiliate exception would defeat the ASSIGN fallback, but that is a different rule and is not a LICENSE defect. No duplicate affiliate coverage arises because "Client" is defined as a single named entity.

Intent is preserved: the successor right is implemented as a Client-only exception rather than a new Vendor assignment exception or a broad "notwithstanding" override, so the consent mechanic, its mutuality, and all other commercial terms survive without contradiction; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created.

Drafting nit (not a failure): after inserting "and, upon written notice to TrueLink, its affiliates", the antecedent of "its business" in "in the ordinary course of its business" is slightly ambiguous; consider "in the ordinary course of their respective businesses" for clarity. Also consider defining or lower-casing "affiliates" consistently, since the agreement uses "affiliate" in § 15 without a definition.
